messages.content: Return only JSON matching the schema. Review this candidate conclusion against the frozen facts. Candidate: 'An EVM smart-contract wallet is necessary but radically insufficient for Article 50 and Code conformance, serving as the durable identity/authorization anchor, third-party delegation record, supplemental log, and x402 settlement boundary while other services mark, watermark, detect, disclose and monitor.' Frozen facts: Article 50 and the final Code require content-level marking/detection and some natural-person disclosures. They permit digitally signed metadata, imperceptible watermarking, optional supplemental logging/fingerprinting, and third-party providers. Neither Article 50 nor the Code requires blockchain, EVM, token custody, payment, x402, or one wallet per legal/organizational unit. C2PA currently uses X.509 signing credentials. An EVM wallet can optionally provide stable address, contract authorization logic, signatures, token custody and settlement, but does not by itself bind a legal identity, mark content, disclose to people, or prove the asserted pipeline event. Local enterprise law requires sovereign boundaries and separately contracted imports but does not require those boundaries to be EVM accounts. Determine whether 'necessary' is warranted, identify any other overclaims, and supply a corrected one-sentence conclusion. This is semantic review, not legal advice.
